headline: GPT-6 shakes the AI world as US midterm mail-vote battle heats up, while MSFT dips 2% last night and PLS slips at today's ASX close.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft slid 2% last night on NASDAQ — a rough session likely driven by investors rotating out of big-tech heavyweights after the frenzy around GPT-6's launch put OpenAI (not Microsoft) in the spotlight. Still up 12.8% overall on your cost base — the long-term AI thesis remains very much intact.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS dropped 2.1% at today's ASX close, part of a broader sell-off hitting lithium stocks. There's no single news catalyst — it's ongoing market caution about lithium demand and pricing. The stock is down 24.5% on your cost base, which stings, but the longer-term case for lithium in the energy transition is unchanged.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: GXAI bounced 1.6% at today's close — riding enthusiasm around the GPT-6 Astra launch and the broader wave of new AI model releases from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Meta this week. Good momentum for a holding that's still 13% below your cost base.

movers.name: Alphabet (Google)
movers.note: Google dipped 1.1% last night — ironic given Google also released new Gemini models this week. The market seems to be rewarding OpenAI's GPT-6 narrative more than Google's efforts right now. Fundamentals remain solid; dividend and cloud growth are holding the valuation up.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two edged up 0.3% last night — quiet session, with GTA 6 PC release speculation providing a gentle tailwind. Reports suggest rising console prices may pressure Rockstar to bring the PC version sooner than expected, which is good news for the long-term revenue story.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS ticked up 0.4% at today's ASX close, tracking the general resilience of the broader US market. Up 2.6% on your cost base — steady as she goes.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG nudged up 0.2% today — a quiet, steady session for this diversified fund. Barely above your cost base but doing its job as a long-term, low-drama hold.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE crept up 0.1% today — essentially flat. Emerging markets have been treading water, and this one is marginally in the red overall (-0.7% on cost). Nothing to worry about for a long-term holder.

watch_today.title: PLS: Lithium sell-off continues — sit tight
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals closed down another 2.1% today, and is now 24.5% below your cost base. There's no company-specific blow-up — it's sector-wide pressure on lithium stocks as the market stays cautious on near-term demand. The long-term energy transition story for lithium is intact. For a buy-and-hold investor this is uncomfortable but not a reason to sell.

watch_today.title: MSFT: Big dip last night — long-term story unchanged
watch_today.detail: Microsoft fell 2% on NASDAQ last night, possibly as market attention shifted to OpenAI's GPT-6 launch rather than Microsoft's own AI products. That's short-term noise. MSFT is still up nearly 13% on your cost base and remains one of the strongest AI infrastructure plays around. Hold firmly.

watch_today.title: GXAI: AI wave giving it a lift — keep holding
watch_today.detail: Your Global X AI ETF rose 1.6% today on the back of a massive week for AI model releases — GPT-6 Astra, new Gemini, Claude Fable 5.1, and Meta models all dropped this week. Still 13% below cost, but the tailwind is real and building. This is exactly the kind of environment this ETF was built for.

watch_today.title: RBA rate hike looming — watch your mortgage and property exposure
watch_today.detail: UBS and Capital Economics are now both tipping the RBA will hike rates at its September meeting. The RBA itself flagged rent prices are keeping inflation sticky. A former RBA official is forecasting a 10% drop in house prices if hikes continue. This is worth watching if you have a mortgage or property holdings outside this portfolio.

watch_today.title: GOOG: Down last night but fundamentals solid — hold
watch_today.detail: Google slipped 1.1% last night as GPT-6 dominated the AI headlines. But Alphabet's own Gemini refresh, strong cloud growth, and its dividend support the valuation. You're still up 9% on cost. No reason to move — this is just competition noise in a fast-moving space.

watch_today.title: TTWO: GTA 6 PC timeline could be a catalyst to watch
watch_today.detail: Reports surfaced that rising console prices may push Rockstar to release GTA 6 on PC sooner than originally planned. That's a potential revenue upside for Take-Two. Nothing confirmed, but worth keeping an eye on. You're currently 7.5% below cost — patient holding looks right here.

world.summary: The biggest global stories today centre on the US midterm election mail-vote battle reaching the Supreme Court, and the ongoing US-Iran conflict dominating Middle East headlines.

stories.title: US courts block Trump's mail-in voting restrictions as midterms begin
stories.why_it_matters: A federal judge has extended a block on a Trump administration order that would have required voters to provide proof of citizenship to vote by mail in the upcoming US midterm elections. The Trump administration is now asking the Supreme Court to step in and clear the way for the rule. Meanwhile, North Carolina has already begun distributing mail ballots under existing rules. This is shaping up to be a major constitutional fight over voting access — and the outcome could influence which party controls Congress after the midterms.

stories.title: US-Iran conflict: How could it end? Experts weigh in as Vance plays down 'war' label
stories.why_it_matters: US Vice President JD Vance said he 'wouldn't call it a war' with Iran, even as the conflict continues. Vance also said he was 'extremely skeptical' that a recent US strike hit an Iranian wedding party — a claim causing significant controversy. Three experts speaking to the BBC offered different views on how the conflict could end: diplomatic deal, Iranian regime change, or a prolonged stalemate. For everyday Australians, the conflict matters because it keeps oil prices elevated and creates global economic uncertainty.

stories.title: Middle East war drives 35% surge in overseas help requests from Hongkongers
stories.why_it_matters: Hong Kong's government says requests from citizens overseas for consular help have jumped 35% since the Middle East conflict escalated. It's a striking human measure of how the war is rippling beyond the immediate region — thousands of people caught up in a conflict far from home, needing evacuation assistance or emergency support. It also signals how globally interconnected the fallout from the Iran conflict has become.

stories.title: Israel, Iran, and the Middle East: live conflict updates
stories.why_it_matters: Fighting between Israel and Iran-backed forces is continuing, with the Jerusalem Post running live updates on the situation. The conflict remains fluid and dangerous — any escalation risks drawing in more regional players and pushing oil prices higher. As a market watcher, elevated oil (currently around USD $91.50/barrel) is already feeding into global inflation.

stories.title: US midterms underway: North Carolina first to distribute mail ballots
stories.why_it_matters: North Carolina has become the first US state to begin distributing mail-in ballots for the 2026 midterm elections, even as the legal battle over mail voting rules rages in the courts. The midterms will determine control of the US House and Senate — which could significantly shape economic policy, trade, and the regulatory environment for tech companies that make up a large chunk of your portfolio.

markets.summary: The ASX 200 edged slightly lower today, closing at 9,005 — down a modest 0.16% in a quiet session. Last night on Wall Street, the S&P 500 dipped 0.38% and the NASDAQ slipped 0.29%, with big tech like MSFT and GOOG both in the red. Gold pulled back sharply by 1.4%, while oil held steady just above $91. The Aussie dollar was essentially flat at around 72 US cents.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Slight dip today — subdued session on the ASX.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Last night's session saw a mild pullback as big tech dragged.

indicators.name: NASDAQ
indicators.note: Tech stocks soft last night despite the AI model launch frenzy.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Oil ticked up slightly, staying elevated amid Middle East tensions.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Gold pulled back sharply — possibly profit-taking after recent highs.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: The Aussie dollar was virtually flat — hovering around 72 US cents.

politics.summary: The big domestic story is the growing likelihood of an RBA interest rate hike in September, with warnings about house prices and ongoing criticism of the Albanese government's handling of veterans.

stories.title: UBS and Capital Economics tip RBA rate hike in September
stories.why_it_matters: Two major financial institutions — UBS and Capital Economics — are now predicting the Reserve Bank of Australia will raise interest rates at its September meeting. The RBA has flagged that rent prices are keeping inflation stubbornly high. If rates go up, that means higher mortgage repayments for millions of Australians and further pressure on the property market — bad news for borrowers, but potentially good for savers and term deposits.

stories.title: Ex-RBA official warns of 10% house price drop
stories.why_it_matters: A former Reserve Bank of Australia official has gone public with a forecast that Australian house prices could fall by as much as 10% if the rate hike cycle continues. That's a significant warning from someone who has worked inside the institution. For Gold Coast homeowners or property investors, this is worth taking seriously — particularly if more hikes are on the way.

stories.title: RBA's inflation view 'disconnected from Australians' lived experience'
stories.why_it_matters: The New Daily argues that the RBA's technical measure of inflation doesn't capture what everyday Australians are experiencing at the shops, the petrol station, or paying rent. Critics say the central bank is looking at smoothed averages while real people are being squeezed hard right now. It's a growing political pressure point for both the RBA and the Albanese government heading into an election cycle.

stories.title: Veterans groups slam 'appalling' treatment by Albanese government
stories.why_it_matters: Veterans' advocacy groups are publicly accusing the Albanese government of failing returned service men and women, describing their treatment as 'appalling.' The criticism centres on delays and inadequacies in veteran support services. With a federal election on the horizon, veteran welfare is a politically sensitive issue — particularly in regional and defence-heavy electorates.

ai.summary: This week has been one of the biggest in AI history — OpenAI dropped GPT-6 Astra and claimed we've entered the 'AGI era', while Anthropic, Google and Meta also all launched major new models. It's a firehose of AI news.

stories.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6 Astra, declares the 'AGI era' has arrived
stories.why_it_matters: OpenAI has released GPT-6 Astra — its most powerful model yet — and is boldly claiming it marks the beginning of the 'AGI era' (AGI = Artificial General Intelligence, meaning AI that can perform any intellectual task a human can). The model features major leaps in reasoning, coding, and the ability to control computers directly. It's priced at about 2.5 times the cost of the previous generation, signalling OpenAI is betting that businesses will pay a premium for genuinely smarter AI. This is the biggest AI product launch in years and directly impacts your GOOG and GXAI holdings.

stories.title: Anthropic, Google and Meta all ship major new models in the same week
stories.why_it_matters: The same week GPT-6 dropped, Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.1, Google pushed out new Gemini models, and Meta launched its own updates — all within days of each other. The article notes they all share one catch: they're getting very expensive to run. The AI arms race is intensifying, which is a tailwind for your GXAI ETF (which holds companies across the AI supply chain) but also signals rising costs that could eventually squeeze profit margins.

stories.title: iOS 27 could let users swap ChatGPT for Gemini or Claude in Apple Intelligence
stories.why_it_matters: Reports suggest Apple's upcoming iOS 27 may allow iPhone users to choose between ChatGPT, Google Gemini, or Anthropic's Claude as the AI brain behind Apple Intelligence — rather than being locked into one provider. That's a big deal: it would turn Apple's billion-plus device install base into an open marketplace for AI assistants, and could significantly boost adoption for Google's Gemini. Good news for your GOOG holding if it plays out.

stories.title: G20 backs light-touch AI regulation as global governance debate continues
stories.why_it_matters: G20 nations have backed a 'light-touch' approach to regulating AI — meaning most major economies are choosing not to impose heavy rules on AI companies, at least for now. This is good news for AI firms like Google, Microsoft, and OpenAI, as it gives them room to move fast without getting bogged down in red tape. For investors in GOOG, MSFT, or GXAI, fewer regulatory headwinds is a positive backdrop.

sport.summary: NRL Round 27 is in full swing — the Broncos thumped the Bulldogs on Thursday, the Dolphins edged the Titans in a controversial game on Friday, and the Rabbitohs hammered the Roosters 50-20 on an emotional night. AFL finals fever is also building with Geelong's Patrick Dangerfield making headlines.

stories.title: Rabbitohs thrash Roosters 50-20 in emotional Jai Arrow tribute night
stories.why_it_matters: South Sydney ran riot at Allianz Stadium, belting the Roosters 50-20 in what was described as an emotion-charged night centred around support for Jai Arrow. The NRL world rallied around Arrow, and the Rabbitohs delivered on the field in emphatic fashion — it's one of the results of the round.

stories.title: Dolphins edge Titans 24-20 in controversy-filled match — NRL great erupts
stories.why_it_matters: The Dolphins beat the Gold Coast Titans 24-20 at Cbus Super Stadium on Friday night, but the result was overshadowed by a refereeing call that had at least one NRL great furious. A controversial decision late in the match swung momentum and the outcome — locals on the Gold Coast will have plenty to say about this one.

stories.title: Broncos belt Bulldogs 34-20 in Round 27 opener
stories.why_it_matters: Brisbane opened Round 27 with a convincing 34-20 win over Canterbury at Accor Stadium on Thursday night. The Broncos continue to build form at the right end of the season, while the Bulldogs will be licking their wounds heading into the final stretch of the regular season.

stories.title: Warriors pip Sea Eagles 31-30 in thriller at Go Media Stadium
stories.why_it_matters: The New Zealand Warriors held on to beat Manly 31-30 in a nail-biting game in Auckland on Saturday afternoon. One point in it — a match that went right down to the wire. Both teams are fighting for finals spots, making this result significant for the end-of-season ladder.

stories.title: AFL: Patrick Dangerfield and Geelong's historic comeback stuns footy world
stories.why_it_matters: Patrick Dangerfield produced a moment that has the AFL world talking, as Geelong pulled off what's being described as a historic comeback. The finals are fast approaching and Geelong appear to be hitting form at exactly the right time. Dangerfield's act — whatever it was — has sparked debate and admiration across the football community.
